analysis:
Examined the whole PR, including the replayed source. It replaces the read-then-hash loop in WeightHasher.hashSingleFileUncached (WeightHasher.swift ~243-258) with the new OverlappedFileDigest.swift. Changelog, configuration.md and model-registry-format.md changes are documentation only. Tests were extended.

Handoff protocol (OverlappedFileDigest.swift 36-88): both `free` semaphores are signaled at start. The reader waits on free[slot], preads at an explicit offset, retries on EINTR, stores the length, and signals filled[slot]. It stops on count<=0. The hasher waits on filled[slot] and hashes exactly `count` bytes in order. count<0 returns nil, so the existing fallback readers run and the path fails closed. A read error cannot yield a truncated digest accepted as valid. Short preads are handled because the offset advances by the actual count. Each buffer is owned by one side at a time, and lengths[] is ordered by the semaphore handoffs. The `defer readerExited.wait()` guarantees the reader has stopped before the caller closes the descriptor. No semaphore ends below its initial value. The digest is the same SHA-256 over the same bytes. Per-file combination (hashFilesWithRelativeKey) and the PageCache.drop step are unchanged.

Security relevance: weight-integrity controls (A-004, T-012, T-027) and the weightHash binding that T-041 relies on are preserved. Memory is bounded at 8 MiB per file being hashed. The buffers hold weights only, not consumer prompts. One short-lived thread is created per file. No change to authorization, attestation, keys, wire protocol, cache encryption or the TB-011/TB-012/TB-013 boundaries. Tests cover chunk boundaries, buffer wrap, chunk-order distinguishing payloads and concurrent readers. Remaining unverified: native F_NOCACHE+pread behavior on Apple hardware, and unchanged callers of WeightHasher. A failure there would fall back to existing readers. No regression identified.
